name: mixed-imitation-pilot-v1
label: descriptive pilot, training side for Room 2; no confirmatory claim; the Room 2 v2 held-out set is never read
question: Does cloning a Room 1 policy on Room 1 and Room 2 demonstrations together, each room weighted equally, keep its Room 1 held-out skill, where Room 2-only cloning erased it (retention pilot)? And does PPO on Room 2 afterwards wear that skill down?
decisions_it_may_inform: whether mixing at the imitation step is enough, or the next step needs mixed PPO (each episode picks a room; new multi-room training code and a review)
the rough size of the Room 1 effect, for a later power estimate
decisions_it_may_not_inform: anything else, including which seeds, clone seeds, checkpoints, mixing ratio or Room 2 settings a later experiment uses; one striking run does not set the next design
changed_from_retention_pilot: only the imitation data and its weighting: the Room 1 demonstrations are added and each room gets the same total weight in the cloning loss. Everything else is held fixed.

held_fixed.donors: config/retention-pilot.json donors: Room 1 varied-start seeds 3 to 6, same checkpoints and sha256, same before values
held_fixed.room2_data: runs/clone/chapter-1-room-2/20260924-014351/dataset.npz with config/demonstrations-room2-v2.json and config/heldout_starts-room2-v2.json (overlap check only); split alone with seed k, so the same 5 held-back Room 2 routes as the retention pilot's R-k and H2's B-k
held_fixed.fine_tuning: the retention pilot's R-k command with --init-from <M-k clone> and --run-dir runs/train/mixed-imitation-pilot-M-k<k>: rew-v2, shaping 2.0, 500,000 steps, checkpoints every 100,000, --stall-frames 296, --seed 40 + k, Room 2 canonical starts only
held_fixed.measurement_commands: Room 1 held-out: scripts/evaluate_heldout.py --checkpoint <zip> --starts config/heldout_starts.json --repeats 1 --seed 20260920 (aggregates only); Room 2 canonical: scripts/evaluate_checkpoint.py --task-definition config/room2.json --episodes 50 --seed 20260924 --reward-version rew-v2 --shaping-scale 2.0

room1_data.why_rerecorded: the existing Room 1 clone dataset (runs/clone/20260918-183508/dataset.npz) predates dataset manifests, so a verified --mix-room refit refuses it
room1_data.procedure: before any pilot data: scripts/clone_room1.py --demonstrations config/demonstrations.json --heldout config/heldout_starts.json --routes-only --no-play (Room 1 default task), which replays the 7 route demonstrations and writes dataset.npz with its manifest; the recorded frames are compared with the old dataset (equal counts and arrays expected; any difference is reported and stops the pilot). DONE 2026-09-25 22:11 to 22:16 at bbb3d69 (log runs/clone-logs/room1-rerecord-20260925.log): all 7 routes replayed to success, 2,688 frames, every array identical to the old dataset; the incidental seed-0 clone equals the original Room 1 clone runs/clone/20260918-183508 in all 36 tensors
room1_data.split: Room 1 is split alone with seed k: 2 of its 7 routes held back

runs.design: M-k for k = 0 to 3: donor seed 3 + k; mixed clone seed k; fine-tuning seed 40 + k. Nominally paired with the retention pilot's R-k (identical except the added Room 1 data and the weighting) and with H2 B-k.
runs.clone_command: scripts/clone_room1.py --task-definition config/room2.json --dataset runs/clone/chapter-1-room-2/20260924-014351/dataset.npz --demonstrations config/demonstrations-room2-v2.json --heldout config/heldout_starts-room2-v2.json --mix-room default config/demonstrations.json config/heldout_starts.json runs/clone/20260925-221134/dataset.npz --room-weighting equal --routes-only --holdout 0.25 --epochs 300 --batch-size 64 --learning-rate 0.001 --no-play --seed <k> --init-from <donor> --init-from-sha256 <donor sha256>
runs.plans: clones fitted by hand with a durable log; then a mechanically generated, committed training plan pinning the four clone hashes (dry run first); then a committed evaluation plan pinning every checkpoint

measurements.primary_room1: Room 1 held-out route-macro and state-weighted success for every M-k clone and every step checkpoint (100k to 500k), all evaluated, no best checkpoint; drop from the donor's before value; retained share (after - floor) / (before - floor)
measurements.floor: the retention pilot's floor, reused: the same 8 checkpoints (H2 B-k0 to B-k3 clones and finals) with the same command, already evaluated (docs/results/retention-pilot.json); clone floor for the post-clone point, final floor for the fine-tuned points
measurements.comparison: the retention pilot's R-k curve at every point (same donors, seeds and Room 2 data; only the mixing differs), described across the four runs
measurements.per_room_imitation: held-back input and frame accuracy per room for each M-k clone (recorded by clone_room1.py): Room 2 against the R-k clone (same seed, Room 2 only), Room 1 against the donor's own accuracy on the same Room 1 held-back frames before cloning
measurements.secondary_room2: descriptive: Room 2 canonical clears of 50 for each M-k clone and final; training clear rate per 100k window and first 50k window at 50%, beside R-k and H2 B-k
measurements.critic_record: explained variance over the first 10 PPO updates for M-k beside R-k

aggregates_only: The Room 1 held-out set already carries the published Phase 3B result and the retention pilot; only aggregate success per checkpoint is reported, never per-route or per-state results.
declared_confounds: Critic: the Room 1 value head is copied with the weights, as in the retention pilot.

Room 1 demonstrations are only 7 routes (5 fitted per clone), against 16 fitted Room 2 routes; equal weighting gives each Room 1 frame about 4 times the weight of a Room 2 frame (the exact ratio depends on each seed's split and is recorded per clone).
The Room 1 demonstrations and the donors' original clone came from the same 7 routes, so the donors have already been fitted to them once; mixing may partly act as a reminder of data they saw.
Single checkpoints swing by a few points (about 3 points of sampling noise at 20% success); describe patterns across the four runs.
later: Before any confirmatory retention experiment, generate a fresh Room 1 held-out set with the existing procedure (--exclude-heldout config/heldout_starts.json) and commit its plan first.
cost: Room 1 re-record a few minutes live; 4 mixed clones about 15 minutes each on CPU; 4 fine-tuning runs about 35 minutes each; 24 Room 1 and 8 Room 2 evaluations about 1.1 hours. About 4.5 hours in total. Plus about 10 minutes for the imitation-only reference (3 CPU refits and 4 evaluations).

imitation_only_reference.why: Phase 3B found the Room 1 clone copied the demonstrations poorly (below a persistence baseline on held-out routes); the donors' Room 1 skill came from PPO on top of it, and no Room 1 clone had ever been scored on the Room 1 held-out set. This reference says what imitating the Room 1 demonstrations alone achieves, so a mixed clone at that level is read as relearning the demonstrations, not keeping the donor's skill.
imitation_only_reference.clones: Room 1-only clones from fresh weights: seed 0 is the existing runs/clone/20260918-183508/cloned.zip (the re-recorded dataset's seed-0 refit is identical in all 36 tensors); seeds 1 to 3 refitted offline with scripts/clone_room1.py --dataset runs/clone/20260925-221134/dataset.npz --demonstrations config/demonstrations.json --heldout config/heldout_starts.json --routes-only --holdout 0.25 --epochs 300 --batch-size 64 --learning-rate 0.001 --no-play --seed <k> (Room 1 default task)
imitation_only_reference.measure: the primary Room 1 command on each of the 4; reported as the mean and range; included in the committed evaluation plan

room2_side_effects: Balanced mixing changes the Room 2 side as well: Room 2 frames carry half the cloning loss instead of all of it; each epoch has about 26% more frames (7,520 Room 2 plus 1,948 Room 1 training frames for seed 0), so there are more gradient steps; and the minibatch order differs. Any Room 2 difference against R-k therefore cannot be attributed to Room 1 being present.
floor_reuse_check: Before any evaluation, confirm that scripts/evaluate_heldout.py and every celeste_rl module it imports are unchanged since f26914d (the floor's evaluation commit); if anything changed, re-evaluate the floor in the same plan. Checked 2026-09-25 at d20f80b: only celeste_rl/cloning.py changed, and nothing the evaluator imports uses it.

decision_branches.measure: Room 1 route-macro retained share against the floor, (after - floor) / (before - floor), and the distance to the imitation-only reference mean, described across the four runs
rules_in_order: A (mixing keeps the skill): after mixed cloning, the median retained share is at least 0.5 and at least 3 of 4 runs are more than 10 points above the imitation-only reference mean. Then, if the median retained share at 500k is at least 0.25 lower than after cloning, the next step is mixed PPO (each episode picks a room; new code and a review); otherwise mixed imitation suffices for these two rooms for now.

B (mixing relearns the demonstrations): not A, and at least 3 of 4 runs after mixed cloning are within 10 points of the imitation-only reference mean. The next step is a recipe whose target is the donor's own play, such as self-distillation (record the donor's actions on Room 1 states and mix those in).

C (mixing did not help): not A or B, and the median retained share after mixed cloning is below 0.2. Mixing at this weight did not help; the owner and the orchestrator choose between self-distillation and a different weight.
D (unclear): anything else is reported descriptively and taken to the orchestrator and the owner; no branch is picked after the fact.

generator_checks: The training-plan generator selects exactly one clone per k by donor sha256, seed k, a clean commit, 300 epochs and mix.room_weighting equal (the clone command must include --room-weighting equal, whose default is frames); the smoke-test clone runs/clone/chapter-1-room-2/20260925-221717 (1 epoch) can never match.
